title: Why money laundering bail is almost as tough as NDPS bail
p1:
Getting bail in a money laundering case is not like getting bail in an ordinary criminal matter.

Many people are surprised to know that the law creates a much higher hurdle before an accused can be released.
p2:
The common misconception is that bail depends only on whether the person looks guilty or innocent at the first stage. But in money laundering cases, courts must consider a stricter test before granting bail.

A special rule requires the court to be satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and is unlikely to commit another offence while on bail.
p3:
This is similar to the approach seen in NDPS cases, where strict bail conditions exist because of the seriousness of the allegations.

The key point many miss: even before a full trial begins, the accused may face a difficult battle to secure freedom. That is why legal strategy, evidence analysis, and understanding the investigation record become crucial from the beginning.
conclusion: Do you think strict bail laws help prevent financial crimes, or do they risk making it harder for innocent people to get relief? Share your view.
